explain.say: Switch on coil A and it pulls the nearest rotor teeth into line. Switch to coil B and the teeth are pulled along by one small step, typically 1.8 degrees.

faq.q: How does a stepper motor work?
faq.a: Electromagnet coils around a toothed rotor are switched on one after another. Each switch pulls the rotor teeth to the next position, moving it by one small, exact step.

faq.q: How many steps does a stepper motor have?
faq.a: The most common type has 200 steps per turn, 1.8 degrees each. Drivers can also split each step into smaller microsteps for smoother, finer movement.

faq.q: Why don't stepper motors need a position sensor?
faq.a: Each pulse moves exactly one step, so counting pulses tells you the position. That is open-loop control, and it works as long as the motor is not overloaded.
asks: How does a stepper know where it is?

faq.q: What happens if a stepper motor skips steps?
faq.a: If the load is too heavy or it is driven too fast, the rotor can't keep up and misses steps. The controller doesn't know, so the position is wrong, which can shift the layers of a 3D print.

faq.q: What is the difference between a stepper and a servo?
faq.a: A stepper moves in counted steps without checking and holds firmly when stopped. A servo uses a sensor and feedback to reach any angle, and corrects itself if pushed.

facts: The most common hybrid stepper motors move 1.8 degrees per step, 200 steps per revolution.
Microstepping drivers can divide each full step into 16 or more smaller steps.

quiz.say: A stepper motor moves 1.8 degrees per step. How many steps make a full turn?
quiz.show: 1.8 degrees per step: steps per turn?
quiz.why: 360 degrees divided by 1.8 degrees per step is 200 steps.

wrong.2: 360 steps would turn 648 degrees, almost two turns.
